summary: Portrait picker dispatches by CLASS index (reads DGROUP 0x560f = class byte). Each of 14 classes has exactly 5 portrait reference values passed to the picker UI. The stored portraitIndex at pcfile +0x1ab is computed as SPD+1 (not player-selected). Cross-validated against all 6 stock characters: 100% match.

findings.claim: Portrait picker at wpcmk 0x3c49 dispatches by class index. It reads the class byte from DGROUP 0x560f (= char_base + 0x19f), then jumps to one of 14 class-specific cases.

disassembly: a0 0f 56    ; mov al, [0x560f]   ; class index (DGROUP 0x560f = char_base+0x19f)
e9 af 01    ; jmp 0x3e06         ; dispatch to 14-class jump table

findings.claim: Each class has exactly 5 portrait reference values. The dispatch calls function 0x3bfb with 5 pushed values; that function iterates them and renders non-zero ones.

evidence.pattern: 5x (b8 XX XX 50) followed by e8 XX XX = mov/push x5 then call

findings.claim: The stored portraitIndex (at pcfile +0x1ab = DGROUP 0x561b) is computed as SPD+1. The player does NOT select the portrait index; it is derived from SPD after the stat roll.

disassembly: a0 a1 55    ; mov al, [0x55a1]   ; SPD byte (char_base+0x131)
fe c0       ; inc al             ; portraitIndex = SPD + 1

findings.claim: portraitIndex == SPD + 1 for all 6 stock characters in pcfile.dbs

unresolved: The encoding of the 5 portrait reference values per class (e.g., Fighter [141, 130, 132, 135, 8]) — what these numbers represent internally (msg IDs? file slot IDs? global portrait indices?). The display function at 0x3aec uses them but its full logic requires runtime trace to decode.

Whether portraitIndex is clamped to 0..13 downstream. Stock chars max SPD=12 (portraitIndex=13), so the ceiling behavior at SPD≥13 is untested. The doc says '14 portraits per file' implying max valid index = 13.

The portrait picker UI at 0x0df7 shows 5 options and lets the player choose — but the CHOSEN portrait's reference value does NOT directly become the stored index. The SPD+1 formula is a post-hoc assignment. It's unclear whether the player's visual selection affects anything other than what's shown on screen during creation (the stored value comes from SPD regardless).
